items.title: Introducing the SpiceDB Playground Assistant
items.summary: We've added an AI assistant to the SpiceDB Playground. It writes and edits your schema, generates relationship data and assertions to test it, runs permission checks, and explains exactly why a check was granted or denied.

items.title: How SpiceDB Secures Authorization for AI
items.summary: AI agents don't make authorization decisions. SpiceDB does. Here's how relationship graphs, consistency guarantees, caveats, and explicit delegation keep every agent action provably scoped.

items.title: Why Large Organizations Need Materialize
items.summary: Materialize continuously maintains precomputed permissions from your SpiceDB permission graph, powering permission-aware search, analytics, RAG, and accelerated checks at large scale.

items.title: Agentic AI Foundation Names AuthZed's Adora Nwodo and Sohan Maheshwar as Ambassadors
items.summary: Adora Nwodo and Sohan Maheshwar from AuthZed have been selected as official ambassadors for the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), joining the program's inaugural cohort.

items.title: Authorization in a Distributed System
items.summary: Problems and solutions when implementing authorization in a distributed system

items.title: Production-grade permissions, half off, exclusively for YC founders
items.summary: AuthZed Cloud is now 50% off for two years for YC-funded companies and companies founded by YC alumni. Here's how to claim it.

items.title: Financial Services and RAG: Join us at Open Source in Finance Forum!
items.summary: The financial industry is leading the way on RAG—and for good reason. Join us at OSFF London on June 25 to see fine-grained authorization for RAG embeddings in action.

items.title: Identiverse 2026: The Conference about Identity's Authorization Problem
items.summary: AuthZed is sponsoring Identiverse 2026, where three of the four featured summits point to the same underlying issue: the assumptions that underpinned IAM for two decades have collapsed, exposing authorization as the missing layer.

items.title: Build and Deploy a GitHub-Style Permission System in AuthZed Cloud
items.summary: Learn how to model a complex GitHub-style permission system with SpiceDB and deploy it to AuthZed Cloud, covering tiered roles, org ownership, team hierarchies, and granular repository permissions.

items.title: Query Planner Early Benchmarks
items.summary: Early benchmarks of the SpiceDB query planner across four schema scenarios and multiple datastore backends, showing where the new planner already outperforms the current dispatch implementation.

items.title: The Culture Panel: Inside AuthZed's Engineering Interview Process
items.summary: Explore AuthZed's culture panel interview - how we assess collaboration, ownership, and team dynamics. Get practical tips on preparing behavioral examples and showcasing your work style.

items.title: Calculate the Authorization Tax: Quantifying the Costs of Home-Grown AuthZ
items.summary: Everyone is paying for authorization. Here are five inputs to help you quantify your Authorization Tax—and two paths to reduce it.

items.title: AuthZed at EIC 2026: Building the Infrastructure Layer for Enterprise AI
items.summary: Next week, AuthZed attends EIC 2026 in Berlin. Stop by Booth #53, join our dinner with Axalon Partners on Tuesday, May 19th, and hear AuthZed CEO Jake Moshenko speak on Thursday, May 21st about treating authorization as shared infrastructure.

items.title: The SpiceDB Playground just got an update
items.summary: We shipped an update to the SpiceDB Playground with a refreshed UI, reworked tab system, and devex improvements. Edit your schema and relationships in the same view without flipping between tabs.

items.title: Build a production-grade Agentic RAG system using AuthZed Cloud
items.summary: Learn how to build a production-grade Agentic RAG system on AuthZed Cloud, where authorization is hardcoded into the LangGraph pipeline—not a prompt instruction the agent can skip.

items.title: Composable Schemas is GA
items.summary: Composable schemas are now generally available in SpiceDB 1.51.1. Split monolithic schemas into well-defined, reusable components so teams can move faster, make changes, and scale without everything becoming entangled.

items.title: Introducing SpiceBox and spicedb-dev
items.summary: AI coding agents need better permissions, and so does the code they write. SpiceBox enforces fine-grained permissions on AI coding agents using SpiceDB, while spicedb-dev gives agents the authorization context they need to generate code with proper access control from the start. Both are open source.

items.title: It's Time to Decompose IAM
items.summary: IAM has never been a single thing—and treating it like one is holding us back. Authentication and authorization are fundamentally different disciplines, and agentic AI might finally force us to address them separately.

items.title: The Technical Skills Panel: Inside AuthZed's Engineering Interview Process
items.summary: Learn how AuthZed's technical skills panel focuses on systems thinking over syntax memorization. Get practical tips on preparing for real-world distributed systems challenges.

items.title: The Background Panel: Inside AuthZed's Engineering Interview Process
items.summary: Discover what AuthZed looks for in the background panel interview - from technical decision-making to ownership and collaboration. Learn how to prepare and showcase your best work.

items.title: Agentic Security and Governance at RSAC and Kubecon
items.summary: Next week, RSAC and KubeCon happen at the same time. While the two shows have very different core audiences, the overlap in topic this year is striking—especially around authorization as a key driver of AI and agentic security.

items.title: An Authorization Platform Built for the AI Era
items.summary: AI agents decide what to access, which tools to call, and what actions to take—autonomously, at volume, and in ways most permission systems weren't designed to handle. AuthZed is the authorization platform built to close that gap.

items.title: Introducing the LangChain SpiceDB Integration
items.summary: We're announcing langchain-spicedb, a new library that brings SpiceDB's relationship-based access control into LangChain and LangGraph workflows. Build RAG pipelines that respect what users are allowed to see with post-retrieval filtering, LangGraph auth nodes, and agent permission tools.

items.title: Feature Highlight: The AuthZed Cloud Datastore, Unlocked
items.summary: AuthZed Cloud customers can now inspect and scale the datastore powering their SpiceDB permission systems directly from the Datastore Overview page.

items.title: Policy Engines Don't Work for AI Authorization. Here's Why
items.summary: Policy engines promise flexible authorization, but they struggle with the ambient context and relationship-driven decisions that AI systems require. Learn why Relationship-Based Access Control (ReBAC) is the better approach for securing AI agents and RAG pipelines.

items.title: Policy Engines for AI Agents
items.summary: Policy engines are being pitched as the solution for AI agent authorization, but they fall short in dynamic, relationship-heavy environments. Jake Moshenko breaks down why relationship-based access control is a better fit as we start treating AI agents more like people than scripts.

items.title: Interact with SpiceDB Seamlessly from within PostgreSQL using the SpiceDB Foreign Data Wrapper
items.summary: Introducing the SpiceDB Foreign Data Wrapper (FDW) for PostgreSQL — a new experimental way to bring real-time authorization context from SpiceDB into Postgres queries, without duplicating data or embedding authorization logic where it doesn't belong.

items.title: Introducing the SpiceDB Query Planner
items.summary: The SpiceDB query planner project explains the architecture on how we're improving the performance of every permission check.

items.title: Try Out AuthZed Cloud, Get AuthZed Cloud Credits
items.summary: The AuthZed Cloud Starter Program provides a $700 credit to try out AuthZed Cloud and see the value of scalable authorization infrastructure.

items.title: The Importance of Off-Sites for a Remote Company
items.summary: While many companies push return-to-office, AuthZed stays remote-first. Our secret is regular off-sites where bonding and business coincide. When we prioritize being human together, we return with more empathy, better communication, and renewed drive to solve hard problems.

items.title: Agentic AI is not Secure
items.summary: MCP, A2A, and ACP standardize how AI agents communicate, but none adequately address authorization. This post analyzes specific vulnerabilities in token granularity, revocation propagation, and delegation chains, and outlines requirements for secure agent infrastructure.

items.title: AuthZed 2025 Year in Review
items.summary: Five years in, our mission remains the same, fixing access control. 2025 was about making our authorization infrastructure available to more teams in more ways.

items.title: MCP is Not Secure
items.summary: MCP standardizes how AI agents connect to tools and data. What it doesn't do is secure them. The spec addresses authentication plumbing but leaves authorization decisions to implementers. So how do you build with MCP without recreating the mistakes behind 2025's breach timeline? It starts with understanding where the protocol ends and your responsibility begins.

items.title: A Timeline of Model Context Protocol (MCP) Security Breaches
items.summary: AI fundamentally changes the interface, but not the fundamentals of security. Here's a timeline of security breaches in MCP Servers from the recent past.

items.title: Build a Multi-Tenant RAG with Fine-Grain Authorization using Motia and SpiceDB
items.summary: Learn how to build a complete retrieval-augmented generation pipeline with multi-tenant authorization using Motia's event-driven framework, OpenAI embeddings, Pinecone vector search, SpiceDB permissions, and natural language querying.

items.title: Terraform and OpenTofu Provider for AuthZed Dedicated
items.summary: AuthZed now supports Terraform and OpenTofu. You can manage service accounts, API tokens, roles, and permission system configuration as code, just like your other infrastructure. Define resources declaratively, version them in git, and automate deployments across environments without manual configuration steps.

items.title: Why we’re not renaming the company AuthZed.ai
items.summary: Should your company rebrand as an AI company? We decided not to. AI companies attract outsized funding and partnership dollars. Yet rebranding means trading established brand value and customer mindshare for alignment with today's hottest trend. We stayed brand-neutral because our authorization solution serves both AI and non-AI companies alike. Limiting ourselves to AI-only would be a disservice to our broader mission and the diverse customers who depend on us.

items.title: AuthZed Dedicated Now Available on Microsoft Azure
items.summary: AuthZed now supports Microsoft Azure, giving customers the opportunity to choose from all major cloud providers - AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. Deploy authorization infrastructure to 23+ Azure regions for globally distributed applications.

items.title: Extended T: Augment your design craft with AI tools
items.summary: How a startup designer makes the T wide, expanding into 3D, rapid iteration, and small-batch production without lowering the quality bar.

items.title: Introducing AuthZed's MCP Servers
items.summary: We're launching two MCP servers to bring SpiceDB closer to your AI workflow. The AuthZed MCP Server provides instant access to documentation and examples, while the SpiceDB Dev MCP Server integrates with your development environment. Learn about our MCP journey from early prototypes to production, and discover how these tools can speed up your SpiceDB development.

items.title: The Dual-Write Problem in SpiceDB: A Deep Dive from Google and Canva Experience
items.summary: In this technical deep-dive, Canva software engineer Artie Shevchenko draws on five years of experience with centralized authorization systems, first with Google's Zanzibar and now with SpiceDB, to tackle one of the most challenging aspects of authorization system implementation: the dual-write problem. This talk was part of the Authorization Infrastructure event hosted by AuthZed on August 20, 2025.

items.title: Turo's SpiceDB Success Story: How the Leading Car-Sharing Platform Transformed Authorization
items.summary: Andre, a software engineer at Turo, shared how the world's leading car-sharing platform solved critical security and scalability challenges by implementing SpiceDB with managed hosting from AuthZed Dedicated. This talk was part of the Authorization Infrastructure event hosted by AuthZed on August 20, 2025.

items.title: AuthZed is 5: What We Learned from Our First Authorization Infrastructure Event
items.summary: We celebrated our 5th birthday with talks from Canva, Turo, and Carnegie Mellon. Here's what we learned about the dual-write problem, scaling authorization in production, and why everyone keeps reimplementing the PostgreSQL wire protocol.

items.title: AuthZed Cloud is Now Available!
items.summary: Bringing the power of AuthZed Dedicated to more with our new shared infrastructure, self-service offering: AuthZed Cloud.
